class: III-Guttural (Lamed-Guttural, ל׳ גרונית: ח, ע, and ה with mappiq; not III-He)
rootNote: Teaching root chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126): H7971 שָׁלַח has 847 verb tokens in 5 stems (Qal 563, Piel 268, Pual 10, Hiphil 5, Niphal 1) and no second weakness. It is the paradigm root of GKC §65 / Paradigm F and Davidson §37. שָׁמַע (1153 tokens) is more frequent but has only Qal/Niphal/Hiphil plus 2 Piel tokens, so it shows fewer of the Piel/Pual furtive-pataḥ forms; לָקַח (964) is excluded because its ל assimilates like a nun (יִקַּח, GKC §66 g). שלח has no Hitpael or Hophal in the Bible; those squares take examples from other III-Guttural roots.
source: Forms from GKC §65 + Paradigm F (Verbs tertiae gutturalis, PDF pp. 477-478) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §37 paradigm (pp. 174-175), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/ and read from page images. Squares those tables do not print follow GKC §65 applied to the strong-verb.json pattern; formBasis says which ('book' = printed in GKC or Davidson; 'rule' = regular pattern). Not copied from any copyrighted chart.
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective ḥolem, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot. Radicals are positional (R1 = שׁ, R2 = ל, R3 = ח); a begadkefat radical's dagesh in dagesh-lene position is optional; Hitpael is matched both with and without sibilant metathesis (הִשְׁתַּ- / הִתְ-). The example's root (with shin/sin dot) was checked against the Strong's headword for its lemma number. Example roots: 3rd radical ח, ע, or ה with mappiq; 1st radical not guttural/נ/י/ו; 2nd radical not guttural/ר/ו/י; not geminate; לקח excluded. Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition (examplePrefix). Example preference: teaching root, then another root of the class; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.furtivePatah: Furtive pataḥ (GKC §22 f, §65.1(a)) is written under the final guttural after ḥireq-yod, ḥolem, shureq, and tone-long ṣere: שְׁלֹחַ, שָׁלוֹחַ, שָׁלוּחַ, שֹׁלֵחַ, הִשְׁלִיחַ, מְשַׁלֵּחַ. It is pronounced before the guttural (shōlēaḥ) and is not a syllable. In this file it is the Unicode pataḥ U+05B7 after the guttural letter, as WLC writes it.
notes.mappiqHe: Verbs with consonantal ה (mappiq) as 3rd radical (גָּבַהּ, תָּמַהּ) inflect like this class (GKC §65 note on the heading; §75 a). They are eligible as examples; III-He verbs without mappiq are a different class.
notes.cohortative: Cohortative = 1st-person yiqtol + ָה: אֶשְׁלְחָה (strong-verb pattern). Shown as a note, not a table row.
notes.jussive: As in the strong verb, the jussive looks like yiqtol except in Hiphil (יַשְׁלַח vs יַשְׁלִיחַ; GKC §65 Rem. 3).
notes.weqatal: וְשָׁלַחְתָּ (regular). Shown as a note, not a column.
notes.pausalForms: In pause, Niphal yiqtol/infinitive and Piel qatal/yiqtol/infinitive often have ṣere + furtive pataḥ (יִשָּׁלֵחַ, שִׁלֵּחַ, יְשַׁלֵּחַ) where the body of the sentence has pataḥ (GKC §65 Rem. 2). Pausal forms are alternates, not main forms.
notes.suffixes: Before the suffixes ךָ and כֶם the guttural takes ḥaṭeph pataḥ (אֶשְׁלָחֲךָ 1 S 16:1; GKC §65.2 Rem.). Suffix forms are not cells.
notes.qalStativeType: III-Guttural statives (e.g. שָׂמַח, שָׂבַע) have the same a-vowel yiqtol (יִשְׂמַח), so no separate stative chart is needed; their perfect may be שָׂבֵעַ. Note only, not cells.
notes.rules: Rules: (1) a final guttural prefers an a-vowel before it: pataḥ replaces ḥolem/ṣere in the last syllable of Qal yiqtol/imperative, Hiphil jussive/wayyiqtol/imperative ms, and (out of pause) Niphal yiqtol and Piel (GKC §65.1(b),(c), Rem. 2-3); (2) unchangeable long vowels (ִי, וֹ, וּ) and the tone-long ṣere of participles are kept and the guttural takes furtive pataḥ (§65.1(a), Rem. 1); (3) 2fs qatal takes a helping pataḥ: שָׁלַחַתְּ (§65.2); (4) a guttural with silent shewa otherwise stays as in the strong verb: שָׁלַחְתָּ.
notes.Hophal imperative: None: GKC Paradigm F and Davidson p. 175 mark it 'wanting'.
